statement: R-006 retains its registered success as a constructed counterexample. Its manual rule inserts the exact positional contrast that F-006 tests. Draw word one from the empirical first-position word list and every other word from the empirical remaining-position list. These lists already encode the length contrast. With the public practice-training paragraph tokens, their EVA-basic means are 4.9359 and 4.4135 glyphs. Nine independent slots imply a first-word excess of 8/9 times their difference, or 0.4643 glyphs against exchangeable line positions. The submitted practice layout shows 0.4456 glyphs above its exact within-line permutation mean. Rotating each line by a uniform random offset preserves its composition and removes the prescribed first position. Across 999 independent rotations the median first-position mean is 4.4509, compared with 4.8988 as submitted. The registered advisory reproduces 4.898773 on the synthetic text and 4.829721 on the manuscript, both passing. A two-list construction shows the contrast is sufficient. It leaves open whether the feature can emerge from a rule whose inputs do not distinguish word one from the other positions.
reproduction: Use the committed attack.json in experiments/R-attack-F-006/fleet-fable and run vs.redteam.run_attack with split practice.

Call corpus.split_pages('practice') and count certain P tokens with dsl.tokens and dsl.select. The training counts are 3431 line-initial tokens and 25934 other tokens. Measure length as len(dsl.SEG(word)) and compute the expectation from the two means.

Retain the publicly laid-out P lines by consuming one submitted synthetic line for every nonempty manuscript line in practice order. This leaves 652 included lines of nine tokens. The exact random-position mean is the mean of all 5868 synthetic positions. Compute 999 simulated whole-line rotations by drawing one length uniformly from each line with random.Random(4086). The 2nd and 98th percentiles are 4.3113 and 4.5767; none reaches the submitted mean.
